page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-32-lssd is a compute-optimized server instance featuring 32 vCPUs and 120 GB of RAM, translating to 3.75 GB of memory per core. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, offering 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The CPU allocation is dedicated, and the processor includes a 504 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. This instance features bundled local storage consisting of 1745 GB of NVMe SSD capacity across 5 local drives, but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in single-threaded operations, with single-threaded gzip compression reaching 36.97 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 15.43 GB/sec. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 2304.0 and an image processing score of 18166.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-threaded performance is also strong, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 18164.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 52401.15. The system demonstrates robust text processing and cryptography capabilities, alongside high throughput for static web serving at 58.17 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 63.56 million operations per second.

Given its dedicated Intel Xeon compute resources and high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, this instance is highly suited for compute-heavy and storage-intensive workloads. The presence of Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) supports specialized tasks like low-latency LLM inference, where it achieves 405.25 tokens/sec for text generation on small 135M models. The qualitative cost efficiency of the c4-standard-32-lssd is driven by its high resource density, combining dedicated compute cores with fast local storage to handle demanding database operations, web serving, and data processing tasks without the overhead of external storage latency.
